title: A Culture of Learning and Promoting Resilience in Multidisciplinary Healthcare Teams
summary:
This study examines the importance of learning culture, resilience and psychological safety among healthcare professionals in outpatient health care systems. An adapted mind-body intervention (BERN - Behaviour, Exercise, Relaxation, Nutrition) is being tested with employees from GP practices.
The aim is to find out whether a video-based mind-body intervention can increase resilience and psychological safety, among other things, and what influence this has on well-being, job satisfaction and learning culture.
conditions: Stress management, promotion of resilience, psychological safety, and a learning culture for healthy (i.e., work-capable) healthcare professionals for all disciplines in primary care in Germany.

interventions.name:
The eight-week mind-body intervention BERN (Behavior, Excercise, Relaxation, Nutrition) aims to facilitate more effective coping with stress.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Included are healthcare professionals (≥ 18 years) within the outpatient healthcare sector (including outpatient clinics and medical care centers) in Germany. Healthcare professionals from general medical and internal medicine practices are included. Voluntary willingness to participate is required.
Exclusion criteria:
Excluded are healthcare professionals of outpatient nursing services, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy practices, as well as other specialist outpatient practices (e.g., pediatrics, cardiology, gynecology). Furthermore, professionals on sick leave or those who are to an employment ban are excluded.
